I farm 225 mu, so I do not run it like a tiny household plot. I have to look at yield, labor, water, and cash together. In Quzhou, wheat-maize is still my main base, so I will start from that and only leave part of the land for cash crops. Last year’s habit matters to me, but I will adjust where the money is worth it. Wheat and maize give me steady grain and keep the rotation familiar. Chili and stevia can bring better cash, but they also need more labor, more spraying, and tighter field management, so I will not put too much area into them. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage and not let the crop sit dry at the key stages. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let the field go hungry, especially on wheat, maize, and chili. I will keep wheat and summer maize on 180 mu of the same land, then I will use 25 mu for chili and 20 mu for stevia. For seed, I will use hybrid maize, improved wheat and stevia, and improved chili seed that people around me have planted with decent results. On tillage, I will plough before wheat and the cash crops to make a clean seedbed, and after wheat harvest I will go with no-tillage maize on the wheat stubble to save time and moisture.
